D.comparison: participants needing more time to integrate skills

O.outcome_detail: perceived value and positive experience of the training

result.effect: 24/28 positive responses; 4/28 needed more time to assess impact

cells.quote: In the post-programme survey, four participants indicated that they needed time to integrate their skills and knowledge to assess the impact of the training programme, whereas all other participants (86%, 24/28) provided a response reflecting a positive experience from the training programme and indicating that it helped them gain valuable communication skills.
cells.note: The study did not include a no-training comparison group; the comparison is between qualitative response categories within the post-programme sample.

D.treatment: opportunity to implement training after returning to practice

O.outcome_detail: self-value, empowerment, self-confidence and job perceptions

cells.quote: Of the 14 participants who were able to implement their training upon returning to practice, the majority expressed feelings of increased self‐value, empowerment and self‐confidence (93%; 13/14): ‘I have felt empowered that I have been able to provide a more positive experience for people and their pets’, and ‘I have gained a new‐found sense of confidence in myself. As well as see[ing] how valuable I am to myself’. Some of these same participants (29%; 4/14) described their job as being more exciting because of being given the chance to work with clients and to use their communication skills: ‘The difficult conversations are much less intimidating now! I am excited to work with clients more and more’.
cells.note: This was a manifest content analysis of 2-month follow-up open-ended responses. The comparison is qualitative: participants unable to implement the training often expressed less-favourable job views, while those able to implement it reported more positive views.
